title: Structural Load Stress Visualization
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive structural load stress visualization for a building frame. The scene must meet ALL of the following requirements:

## Scene Setup
- A perspective camera at position (20, 15, 20) looking at the origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- A ground plane (50x50, gray color #444444) at y=0.
- A grid helper on the ground plane for architectural reference.

## Building Frame Structure
- Construct a 3-story steel frame building using CylinderGeometry for columns and BoxGeometry for beams.
- The frame is a 3x3 grid of columns (4 columns wide x 4 columns deep = 16 columns per floor, 48 total columns across 3 floors). Each floor is 4 units tall. Column spacing is 6 units in both X and Z.
- Beams connect adjacent columns horizontally at each floor level (y=4, y=8, y=12). Use thin box geometry (0.3 x 0.3 cross-section).
- Store all structural members (columns and beams) in arrays for stress computation.
- Each structural member starts with a default material color of steel gray (#888888).

## Load System
- Maintain a list of point loads that can be placed on the roof level (y=12).
- Each load is visualized as a downward red arrow (use ArrowHelper) at the placement point.
- Loads have a magnitude (in kN) starting at 50kN, adjustable via UI.
- Maximum 8 loads can be placed simultaneously.
- Total structural capacity is 800 kN. If total load exceeds capacity, trigger an 'overload' warning state.

## Stress Computation & Visualization
- When loads change, recompute stress on every structural member.
- Stress on a column is proportional to the sum of loads above it, weighted by inverse-square distance from the load's XZ position to the column's XZ position, divided by the column's floor level (lower floors bear more stress).
- Stress ratio = computed_stress / max_allowable_stress (where max_allowable_stress = 200 for columns, 150 for beams).
- Color-map each member: stress ratio 0.0 = green (#00ff00), 0.5 = yellow (#ffff00), 1.0 = red (#ff0000). Use HSL interpolation (hue from 120 to 0 degrees).
- Members exceeding stress ratio 1.0 should pulse/flash red to indicate failure.
- Beams receive stress based on the average stress of their two supporting columns.

## Deformation Visualization
- Toggle-able deformation mode that displaces members proportionally to their stress.
- Columns compress vertically (scale Y reduced by up to 5% at max stress).
- Beams deflect downward at midpoint (translate Y down by up to 0.3 units at max stress).
- Deformation is exaggerated for visibility but proportional to actual stress ratios.

## User Interactions
- LEFT CLICK on the roof plane (y=12) to place a load at that position.
- RIGHT CLICK on an existing load arrow to remove it.
- Press 'D' to toggle deformation visualization on/off.
- Press 'R' to reset all loads (clear everything).
- Press 'U' to undo the last load placement (stack-based undo, up to 8 levels).
- Press 'Y' to redo a previously undone load placement.
- Press '+' or '=' to increase the next load magnitude by 25kN (max 200kN).
- Press '-' to decrease the next load magnitude by 25kN (min 25kN).

## HUD / DOM UI
- A top-left HUD panel (semi-transparent dark background, white text) showing:
  - 'Total Load: XXX kN' (sum of all placed loads)
  - 'Load Count: X / 8'
  - 'Next Load: XXX kN'
  - 'Max Stress Ratio: X.XX' (highest stress ratio among all members)
  - 'Deformation: ON/OFF'
  - 'Status: SAFE / WARNING / OVERLOAD' (SAFE < 0.7 total capacity, WARNING 0.7-1.0, OVERLOAD > 1.0)
- A bottom bar with buttons: [Add Load at Center], [Reset All], [Toggle Deformation], [Undo], [Redo].

## State Management (CRITICAL)
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
  - totalLoad: number (sum of all load magnitudes in kN)
  - loadCount: number (number of active loads)
  - nextLoadMagnitude: number (magnitude for next load placement)
  - maxStressRatio: number (highest stress ratio across all members, rounded to 2 decimal places)
  - avgStressRatio: number (average stress ratio across all members, rounded to 3 decimal places)
  - deformationEnabled: boolean
  - status: string ('SAFE' | 'WARNING' | 'OVERLOAD')
  - undoStackSize: number (number of actions that can be undone)
  - redoStackSize: number (number of actions that can be redone)
  - totalMembers: number (total structural members: columns + beams)
  - failedMembers: number (members with stress ratio > 1.0)
  - columnCount: number (total columns)
  - beamCount: number (total beams)
  - loads: array of objects [{x, z, magnitude}] for each placed load
  - capacityRatio: number (totalLoad / 800, rounded to 3 decimal places)
  - floorStress: array of 3 numbers [floor1_avg, floor2_avg, floor3_avg] average stress ratios per floor
  - conservationCheck: boolean (true if sum of member forces approximately equals total applied load, within 5% tolerance)

Ensure the animation loop runs continuously and __3D_STATE__ is updated every frame.
physics_constraints: Stress distribution follows inverse-square distance weighting from load points. Lower floors bear proportionally more load (divided by floor index from top). Total structural capacity is 800 kN. Stress ratios must be non-negative and NaN-free. Conservation: sum of internal member stresses must approximately equal total applied external load within 5% tolerance. Deformation is proportional to stress ratio. Color mapping uses continuous HSL interpolation from green (0 stress) through yellow (0.5) to red (1.0).
